done_when: Forge runs uv without GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR and GIT_INDEX_FILE, so a merge commit in a linked worktree across a pin change keeps the repo non-bare, its index intact and the merge committed, and a test proves it on new and adopted repos

known.title: Gate: merge-hook proof on earlier-adopted repositories

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test. The Done-when explicitly requires this regression test on new and adopted repositories, but this test only uses a fresh repository. `tests/conftest.py:446` creates that repository from scratch, and `tests/test_close.py:229` supplies no adoption variant. The earlier-adopted cases in `test_running_commands_follow_changed_forge_pin.py` do not install this pre-commit hook or exercise uv's Git operations under its inherited environment. Add an earlier-adopted case to this command-level regression so it also proves the repository remains non-bare, its index intact, and the merge committed after upgrade.
findings.title: Gate: merge-hook proof on earlier-adopted repositories

why: Forge's pre-commit hook hands a merge commit to the pinned release through uv with git's hook variables, and uv's own git init then turns the whole repo bare so no git command works
